title: Before changing the flow, I tested whether users had a strong enough reason to start KYC

children.text: KYC conversion was sitting around 30–33%. The homepage was one of the main entry points, and the copy in that area had been unchanged for some time.
Before adding more changes to the flow, I wanted to isolate one question. Was the way we explained KYC giving users a strong enough reason to begin verification?

We ran the experiment directly in the live mobile product from 12 September to 1 October 2025. The surrounding KYC entry experience stayed largely the same so behavioral differences were easier to read against the messaging itself.

callout: This was not a page redesign. The variable was the reason we gave users to start KYC.

title: We shipped the framing that best matched the job of the entry point

children.text: The homepage did not need to explain the whole KYC experience. Its job was to give eligible users a strong enough reason to enter the flow without attracting traffic that immediately dropped out.
Variant C made the financial value of verification more concrete. Its KYC Start result matched that objective better, while downstream progression did not show a meaningful decline.
Monetary Highlight then replaced the legacy homepage copy in production.

callout: The rollout followed the experiment objective and the strength of the evidence, not simply the highest final number.

title: The experiment showed that the new framing beat legacy, not that Variant C was an absolute winner

children.text: The strongest findings were that every new framing beat the legacy message and that C outperformed A at KYC Start. At the end of the funnel, A, B, and C did not differ significantly from one another.

I therefore would not use the broader KYC uplift after rollout as isolated proof of the copy effect. Other changes, including Autosave and the flexible KYC flow, also entered the experience during the wider improvement period.
The narrower conclusion is more useful. How value is explained at an entry point can change whether users choose to begin a flow before any structural redesign takes place.

title: The next useful experiment would be narrower, not another set of broad variants

children.text: Once the legacy framing had been ruled out, the next question was no longer whether new copy worked. It was which part of the General and Monetary framing was actually moving behavior.

I would narrow the next test to the closest candidates and change one value proposition element at a time. That would make the mechanism easier to understand than testing several broad concepts again.
